## Function

SYNE1 is a very large gene encoding nesprin-1 isoforms. Through the LINC complex, major isoforms connect the nuclear envelope to cytoskeletal systems, contributing to nuclear positioning, mechanics, and cellular organization.

::: {.gene-mechanism}
::: {.gene-state}
**Nesprin-1 network intact**

Mechanical information and nuclear position are coordinated with the cytoskeleton.
:::
::: {.gene-flow-arrow}
→
:::
::: {.gene-state .gene-state-off}
**Relevant isoform lost**

Nuclear architecture, positioning, migration, or mechanotransduction may change—depending strongly on isoform and cell type.
:::
:::

Because SYNE1 is enormous and has many isoforms, “SYNE1 methylated” is underspecified. A CpG may mark one promoter or transcript without silencing the entire locus. Its value in colitis-associated neoplasia may be biomarker-like rather than a direct driver mechanism.

<details><summary><strong>Necessary annotation</strong></summary>

Report exact CpGs, promoter/isoform, transcript expression, nesprin-1 protein localization, and nuclear-shape/mechanics phenotype.
</details>
